stem: Arjun's rhombus has diagonals $6\ \mathrm{cm}$ and $8\ \mathrm{cm}$. Each side is $5\ \mathrm{cm}$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice that uses the diagonals or base and height.

part_answers.answer: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular, so area equals one-half the product of the diagonals: $\tfrac{1}{2}\times 6\times 8=24$.

teacher.key_rationale: With diagonals given, area = ½×d1×d2 = 24. Dropping the ½ doubles the area. Side×side uses the side length as if it alone were an area formula here. Base×height also works when height is known; here the diagonal product is the direct route.
